key_findings: CFA-induced inflammatory pain at P10 (critical window before P12) causes a persistent, non-sex-specific social preference deficit in adult mice without long-term anxiety or altered basal nociception.
Early-life pain reduces ACC CaMKII+ neuron numbers and increases ACC GABAergic neuron numbers, producing an E/I imbalance.
During social approach, ACC CaMKII+ neuron activity and glutamate release are diminished while GABAergic neurons fail to reduce their activity in CFA mice.
Chemogenetic/optogenetic activation of ACC CaMKII+ neurons or inhibition of ACC GABAergic neurons rescues the social deficit; activating ACC GABAergic neurons in naive mice induces it.
Targeted metabolomics showed elevated total glutamate and GABA, arginine and serotonin, and reduced choline and leucine in the ACC of CFA mice.
Intra-ACC CX546 or flumazenil and 66 µA ACC DBS ameliorate the social deficit; DBS activates ACC excitatory neurons.
